messages.subject: Two-level hierarchy
parts:
Dear all,

I am dealing with a two-level hierarchical model. There are two states, and in each state there are 3 cities. I want to test the effect of variable x on the response variable y, but the effect of x will follow the two hierarchies - city/state. The two state share the same hyperparamters, and the 3 cities in each state share the same hyperparameters.

I didn’t find a way to set two-level hierarchy with INLA. So I defined a new index for each specific city (from 1 to 6), and then the model formula became:

formula = y ~ f(x, model="iid", replicate = new_index)

But in this way, these 6 cities are totally independent but share the same hyperparameters, is it correct?

If correct, it is not exactly what I want. Do you know how to deal with this question?

Thanks,
Ruby

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Two-level hierarchy
parts:
sure you cannot just use two iid's, like

f(city...) + f(state...)

?

otherwise, send me the math of your model.
